statement: In an NP the number of the head noun must be compatible with the determinative: this and that agree with the head, and other determinatives select either a singular head (a, each) or a plural head (two, several).
condition: Applies to NPs with a determiner that is a determinative: singular-selecting determinatives (a, each, this, that) combine with a singular count head; plural-selecting determinatives (two, several, these, those) combine with a plural head.
violation: A singular-selecting determinative is followed by a plural head noun, or a plural-selecting determinative by a singular count head noun.

review_notes: The page names a, each, two, several; the rest of the determinatives are in Ch. 5. Non-count heads (e.g. 'much equipment') are outside this record. Compound modifiers ('a two-week trip') are not considered.

statement: Present-tense non-modal verbs, and be in the preterite, agree in person and number with their subject NP, whose person-number classification normally derives from its head noun.
condition: Applies to finite clauses with a present-tense non-modal verb, or with be in the preterite, and a subject NP: the verb's form matches the subject's person and number as determined by the head noun, subject to the listed notional-number departures. Modal auxiliaries are excluded because their present-tense form is invariant across subjects.
violation: A present-tense non-modal verb, or be in the preterite, has a person-number form that does not match the person and number of the subject NP, subject to the listed departures.

exceptions.description: Subjects whose notional number differs from the head noun's form: 'A number of boys were absent' (singular head, plural subject) and 'Three eggs is plenty' (plural head, single-quantity subject). The source says there are 'a good few' such departures.

Modal auxiliaries have one present-tense form with all subjects and do not take a third-person-singular -s ending; they therefore do not participate in the present-tense subject agreement pattern described here.

correct.text: A number of players were injured.
correct.note: Head 'number' is singular but the subject counts as plural.
Plural head, but the subject expresses one quantity.
Modal auxiliary can keeps the same present form with a third-person-singular subject.
Modal auxiliary can keeps the same present form with a plural subject.

review_notes: The rule applies to inflecting present-tense verbs and be in the preterite; modal auxiliaries are excluded because their present form is invariant for person and number (Cambridge Ch. 3 §1.1, p. 75).
